Successful execution of projects like TAP and CASA-1000 will directly impact energy security, trade, and economic development across Central and South Asia.

stories.title: Litton Das Scores Century as Bangladesh Posts 400 Against South Africa
stories.summary:
Bangladesh was bowled out for 400 on the second day of the first Test match against South Africa at the Wanderers Stadium. Resuming their innings at 327 for six, the visiting team added 73 runs to their overnight total before losing their remaining four wickets during the morning session. This score marks Bangladesh's highest ever total in Test cricket against South Africa.

Litton Das, who resumed his innings at 92, reached his eighth Test century by hitting a top-edged pull for a six off bowler Marco Jansen. Das went on to score 120 runs before being caught at midwicket off the bowling of Dane Paterson. Paterson was the most effective bowler for South Africa during the morning, claiming all four of the remaining wickets to finish with figures of four wickets for 92 runs.

The innings featured significant contributions from other batsmen, including Tanzid Hasan, who scored 67 runs, and Towhid Hridoy, who contributed 137 runs. Kagiso Rabada also performed strongly for the South African bowling attack, securing five wickets for 70 runs across the innings, which lasted a total of 101.2 overs.

This performance is significant for Bangladesh as it establishes a new benchmark for their highest innings total against South Africa in the longer format of the game. Reaching the 400-run milestone provides the visiting team with a competitive foundation on the scoreboard as the first Test match progresses.

stories.title: Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina Vows to Return to Bangladesh
stories.summary:
Ousted former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has stated in an email interview with AFP that she intends to return home in December despite facing a threat of death. Hasina, 79, fled to India in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that concluded her 15-year rule. Last year, she was sentenced to death in absentia by a Bangladeshi court after being convicted of crimes against humanity in connection with a deadly crackdown on protesters. 

The announcement follows recent statements from Bangladeshi authorities indicating that she would face execution upon return and has no remaining legal recourse after missing the appeal deadline. Hasina has consistently rejected the legitimacy of the trial. Dhaka has formally requested her extradition from India, a matter that Indian officials state is currently under legal review. Hasina noted that her lawyers have applied for a Bangladeshi passport and national identity card through the high commission in New Delhi to facilitate her homecoming.

Analysts suggest that her declared return is a strategy to maintain political relevance, support her base, and preserve the Awami League party, whose activities are currently banned. Hasina denied allegations that her party was behind recent petrol bomb attacks and asserted she would not request Indian assistance for her travel, emphasizing that extradition is a matter between sovereign states. She also faces over 600 other legal charges, including corruption allegations.

The development matters because Hasina's potential return could significantly impact the political stability and security situation in Bangladesh. Her leadership of the Awami League and the legal implications of her death sentence present major diplomatic and domestic challenges for both Dhaka and New Delhi.

stories.title: Lower Government Borrowing Rates Could Ease Citizen Tax Burdens
stories.summary:
Ordinary citizens and businesses in Pakistan frequently face heavy tax burdens to cover state costs, yet public debt management continues to face scrutiny. With debt servicing consuming 125 percent of Federal Board of Revenue taxes retained by the federal government, 68.5 percent of total revenues, and nearly three times the defense budget, experts argue that avoidable costs should not fall on taxpayers. A major factor in this dynamic involves current accounts, which make up nearly 40 percent of all bank deposits—reaching Rs15.3 trillion by June 2026—on which commercial banks pay no interest. Banks utilize these cheap funds to purchase government securities at exceptionally high returns. Data from the State Bank of Pakistan indicates that banks paid an average interest rate of just 5.53 percent on total deposits in September 2026, while the government borrowed through 12-month treasury bills at 12.79 percent in October 2026, creating a gross difference of 7.26 percentage points.

This gap allows commercial banks to accumulate massive holdings in government securities, totaling Rs40.36 trillion in September 2026, while ordinary taxpayers bear the ultimate cost through levies on petroleum, energy bills, and high income taxes. Applying the gross interest-rate differential yields an estimated annualized figure of approximately Rs2.93 trillion. A proposed legal reform suggests limiting the interest paid to commercial banks on government securities to a reasonable margin of one to two percentage points above average deposit costs. Such a policy could generate annual savings between Rs2,100 billion and Rs2,500 billion, while slightly reducing the State Bank of Pakistan's interest earnings.

Realized savings could be redirected to provide tangible relief to households and struggling entrepreneurs rather than expanding public expenditures. Key proposals include reducing the Petroleum Development Levy and General Sales Tax on electricity bills, doubling the annual income-tax exemption threshold from Rs600,000 to Rs1.2 million for salaried individuals, restoring the Final Tax Regime for exporters at a 2 percent rate, and completely abolishing the super tax while capping corporate income tax at 35 percent. Implementing these changes would help stimulate economic growth, encourage investment, and alleviate poverty by removing excessive taxation on the productive economy.

The author of the proposal is a former federal finance secretary and current chairman of the Policy Research and Advisory Council. Proponents assert that transparency must be maintained by requiring the Ministry of Finance and the State Bank of Pakistan to publish quarterly reports detailing borrowing amounts, interest paid, and actual savings achieved.

stories.title: Federal Constitutional Court Conditionally Permits Peshawar High Court Hearings
stories.summary:
The Federal Constitutional Court modified its earlier directives, conditionally permitting the Peshawar High Court to hear cases concerning the preventive detention of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf workers and activists under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance. Previously, a two-member bench headed by Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan and including Justice Aamer Farooq had barred the Peshawar High Court from hearing these cases on November 5 following the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Under the updated ruling, the high court is allowed to review detention cases on the strict condition that it does not entertain pleas challenging the October 11 proclamation of emergency, governor's rule, or the deployment of the army in aid of civil power.

The legal challenge arose after the Peshawar High Court issued interim orders granting bail to detainees against surety bonds of Rs100,000 each, prompting more than 60 appeals from the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Home and Tribal Affairs Department additional chief secretary. Proceedings had initially been suspended under Article 199 and Article 245 of the Constitution, which restrict high court jurisdiction where armed forces operate in aid of civil power. During proceedings, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa advocate general submitted a report stating that security threats and terrorist networks across the province remain volatile, making the continued deployment of armed forces indispensable and necessitating the protection of executive security actions from premature judicial interference.

During the hearing, the court also allowed PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and the Peshawar Bar Council to join as parties in the proceedings. Barrister Gohar argued that the initial suspension order severely affected legal practice and left numerous PTI workers and activists detained without a constituted review board. While Justice Farooq observed that a strict literal reading of Article 245 would bring the judicial system to a standstill, the provincial advocate general maintained that review boards for detentions exceeding three months would be established subsequently.

The emergency and governor's rule were initially imposed by the federal government on October 11, citing the provincial government's disengagement from counter-terrorism efforts. This political intervention followed heightened tensions and failed negotiations regarding a planned PTI protest march to Islamabad, resulting in the detention of numerous party members and lawmakers, including non-functional Chief Minister Sohail Afridi.

stories.title: Gold and Silver Prices Drop Across Local and International Markets
stories.summary:
Gold prices in Pakistan registered a notable decline, following downward movements in the global market. According to rates provided by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, the local price of gold per tola decreased by Rs2,000 to settle at Rs408,936 during the day. Similarly, the price of 10-gram gold fell by Rs1,715 to be sold at Rs350,596.

This local correction followed a previous session on Saturday when the per tola gold price had reached Rs410,936 after dropping by Rs700. The domestic reductions directly tracked international trends, where the global rate of gold dropped by $20 to reach $3,864 per ounce.

Precious metals saw broad declines alongside gold. Specifically, the price of silver also experienced a downward adjustment, shedding Rs115 to reach a rate of Rs5,228 per tola in the domestic market.

stories.title: ICC Eliminates Super Six Stage for 2027 ODI World Cup Qualifier
stories.summary:
The International Cricket Council has eliminated the Super Six stage from the 2027 ODI World Cup Qualifier, replacing it with a newly structured knockout format for the upcoming ten-team tournament scheduled for February and March next year. Under the revised layout, the ten participating squads will be split into two groups of five teams each. The top two sides from each group will advance directly to the semi-finals, with the winners meeting in the final match. This modification reduces the total number of matches in the Qualifier from 34 down to 23, marking a clear change from the format utilized across the previous three editions.

The governing body confirmed these adjustments following meetings held in Bali. The qualification pathway leading to the 2027 World Cup has also undergone a comprehensive overhaul approved by the ICC Board in July. The winner of the upcoming Qualifier will secure direct entry into the main 14-team World Cup event. Meanwhile, the teams finishing in second, third, and fourth place will advance to the tournament's first round, designated as the Super Series, where the top-performing side will claim the final remaining berth in the main tournament.

Several teams have already secured their positions in the Qualifier based on their rankings or regional competitions. West Indies and Ireland earned their places through their rankings, while the United States, Netherlands, Scotland, and Oman qualified via Cricket World Cup League 2. The remaining four spots will be decided during the Qualifier Playoff in Nepal next month, which will feature the bottom four teams from League 2 alongside four competitors from the third-tier Challenge League.

stories.title: Jay Shah Elected Unopposed For Second Term As ICC Chair
stories.summary:
Jay Shah has secured another two-year term as the chair of the International Cricket Council after being elected unopposed at the governing body's board meeting held in Bali. The announcement was officially made by the ICC on Monday.

Shah previously made history in 2024 by becoming the youngest person to lead the organization when he assumed the role at the age of 35. Prior to heading the international body, he served as the secretary of the Board of Control for Cricket in India. He is also the son of India's home minister, Amit Shah.

During his upcoming second term, Shah will play a central leadership role in managing cricket's official return to the global sporting stage at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games. This milestone marks a significant moment for the administration.

Highlighting the importance of the upcoming Olympic inclusion, Shah emphasized that the event provides an extraordinary platform. He noted it would help introduce the sport to completely new audiences while inspiring an entirely new generation of both players and enthusiastic fans worldwide.

stories.title: Foreign dignitaries gather in Islamabad for the 30th ECO ministerial meeting
stories.summary:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and multiple international delegates arrived in Islamabad to participate in the 30th Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers meeting. Upon landing, the Iranian foreign minister was welcomed at the airport by Additional Foreign Secretary Muhammad Tariq Wazir and other foreign ministry officials. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar hosted a welcome dinner on Sunday for the visiting foreign ministers and delegation heads, emphasizing close bonds among member states and Pakistan's dedication to regional cooperation, peace, and progress.

Diplomatic activity in the capital began on Saturday with the arrival of Tahsin Ertugruloglu, Foreign Minister of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus. Additional high-level arrivals included Turkey's Deputy Foreign Minister and delegation head Musa Kulaklikaya, Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Deputy Secretary General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda, Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, Azerbaijan’s Deputy Foreign Minister Elnur Mammadov, and Kazakhstan’s Deputy Foreign Minister Arman Issagaliyev.

On the sidelines of the summit, Deputy Prime Minister Dar met with ECO Secretary General Dr Asad Majeed Khan. During their discussion, Dar stressed the significance of regional connectivity and economic integration, outlining Pakistan's chairmanship theme, "Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO," and confirming plans to host the ECO Summit in 2027. Dr Khan praised Pakistan's hospitality, arrangements, and coordination for the event.

In a separate meeting, Dar welcomed the OIC secretary general on his maiden visit to Islamabad since taking office. The discussions focused on reinforcing the OIC as a unified voice for the Muslim Ummah. The OIC chief commended Pakistan's diplomatic mediation during the Iran-United States conflict, as well as its active contributions to scientific and technological cooperation through Comstech.

stories.title: Sindh High Court Issues Notices Over Qaim Ali Shah Acquittal Plea
stories.summary:
The Sindh High Court has formally issued notices to the prosecutor general of the National Accountability Bureau and other relevant respondents regarding a review petition filed by former Sindh chief minister Qaim Ali Shah. The court has instructed all respondents to submit their official replies by December 1.

The legal filing follows a previous decision by an accountability court on October 6, which had rejected the former chief minister's initial petition seeking acquittal from the charges brought against him in an ongoing NAB reference case.

In the high court petition, Shah's legal defense argued that the accountability bureau failed to present any verifiable evidence demonstrating monetary benefit or personal corruption related to the executive decisions he made while serving as chief minister.

Furthermore, the petition contended that following the legal amendments enacted in 2022, accountability courts no longer possess the jurisdiction to hear this matter or take punitive action regarding administrative or procedural errors. Consequently, the defense has asked the high court to declare the previous accountability court ruling void and grant full acquittal.

stories.title: Elderly Accident Victim Dies In Karachi Hospital After 20 Days
stories.summary:
An elderly man named Shaheen Baig passed away on Monday while receiving medical treatment in an intensive care unit. He had been battling severe, critical injuries for 20 days following a vehicle collision that occurred near Johar Mor in Karachi on October 17.

The initial accident took place when a car, operated by a clinical psychologist identified as Dr Ayesha Zahid, struck the elderly pedestrian before subsequently colliding with a nearby rickshaw. Funeral prayers for Baig are scheduled to be held at his residence located in Gulistan-e-Jauhar.

In the aftermath of the collision, a chaotic confrontation and heated dispute erupted between the driver and onlookers at the site. Widespread social media attention was drawn to viral video footage depicting the woman arguing, pushing motorcycles, climbing onto vehicle bonnets, and engaging in physical scuffles, which caused major traffic disruptions.

While online speculation questioned whether the driver was intoxicated during the incident, Dr Ayesha strongly denied these claims in a video statement. She explained that she felt unwell due to medication, stepped out to evaluate the damage for potential compensation, and reacted angrily because some of her personal belongings were stolen.

stories.title: میکسیکو میں 40 برس قبل ہونے والا تاریخ کا بدترین گیس دھماکہ
stories.summary:
نومبر 1984 میں میکسیکو سٹی کے مضافاتی قصبے سان خوانیکو میں سرکاری تیل کمپنی پی میکس کے گیس ذخیرہ مرکز پر ایک تباہ کن حادثہ پیش آیا۔ اس المناک واقعے کے نتیجے میں 650 سے زائد افراد لقمہ اجل بنے، আढ़ाई ہزار افراد زخمی ہوئے اور تقریباً 25 ہزار لوگ اپنے گھروں سے محروم ہو گئے۔

حادثے کی صبح گیس کے اخراج سے ایک بڑا بادل بنا جس نے آگ پکڑ لی اور گیس ذخیرہ کرنے والے ٹینکوں میں سلسلہ وار دھماکے شروع ہو گئے۔ اس گیس پلانٹ کے قریب آبادی تیزی سے پھیل چکی تھی اور کچھ گھر تنصیب سے محض 130 میٹر کے فاصلے پر واقع تھے۔ دھماکوں کے نتیجے میں ڈیڑھ کلومیٹر بلند آگ کا ستون آسمان کی طرف اٹھا اور قصبے پر جلتے ہوئے ملبے کی بارش شروع ہو گئی۔

اس وقت چودہ سالہ ورجینیا مارٹینیز اپنے خاندان کے ہمراہ اس علاقے میں مقیم تھیں۔ شدید حرارت، دھوئیں اور خوف کے عالم میں ان کا خاندان پیدل اور اپنی پرانی گاڑی کے ذریعے محفوظ مقام کی طرف نقل مکانی کرنے پر مجبور ہوا۔ اس ہولناک حادثے نے پورے قصبے کو ایک آسیب زدہ اور ویران علاقے میں تبدیل کر دیا تھا جہاں کئی ہفتوں تک عام رسائی ممکن نہ ہو سکی تھی۔

پی میکس نے اس حادثے کی ذمہ داری تسلیم کرتے ہوئے متاثرین کو معاوضہ دینے کا اعلان کیا۔ صحت اور حفاظتی ماہرین کے مطابق یہ سانحہ ناقص شہری منصوبہ بندی، تکنیکی خامیوں اور حفاظتی اصولوں کی سنگین خلاف ورزیوں کا نتیجہ تھا۔ چالیس سال گزرنے کے باوجود اس واقعے کے اثرات اور خوفزدہ کرنے والی یادیں متاثرہ خاندانوں کے ذہنوں میں آج بھی تازہ ہیں۔

stories.title: Bushra Bibi Files Petition Seeking Hospital Transfer Over Health Concerns
stories.summary:
Former first lady Bushra Bibi has filed a fresh petition in the Islamabad High Court through her legal team, Barrister Salman Safdar and Latif Khosa, requesting an immediate transfer from Adiala jail to a specialized medical facility. The filing highlights severe deterioration in her eyesight and warns of the risk of permanent blindness due to inadequate care.

The petition details harsh incarceration conditions, describing her quarters as a large hall-like room with poor sanitation that has resulted in insect infestations. It alleges that bug bites cause painful skin rashes, and notes that jail officials previously killed and removed small snakes from her cell. Medical arrangements at the prison are also criticized, noting that the on-duty doctor is a gynaecologist rather than an eye specialist.

According to the legal filing, Bushra Bibi has been diagnosed with mature cataracts in both eyes and suffers from persistent pain requiring daily painkillers. While doctors previously recommended surgery for November 15, her examination by an ophthalmologist was delayed by seven to eight days. Medical professionals have reportedly warned that post-surgical infections could lead to complete and permanent vision loss, as her current eyesight is so impaired that she can only discern blurred figures.

The legal action follows a November 11 meeting between the former first lady and her lawyers, and comes while she challenges her seven-year prison sentence handed down in January 2025 by an accountability court in the Al-Qadir Trust case. The petitioner has asked the court to summon her complete medical records, secure necessary treatment facilities, and order her transfer for eye surgery.

stories.title: Supreme Court Grants Post-Arrest Bail to Four Suspects in Placenta Smuggling Case
stories.summary:
The Supreme Court of Pakistan has granted post-arrest bail to four suspects involved in an illegal human placenta trading case. A two-member bench, headed by Justice Shahzad Ahmad Khan and including Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi, approved the bail on Monday for three Chinese nationals and one Pakistani citizen against bonds of Rs1 million each and two local sureties. The suspects were initially apprehended by the Federal Investigation Agency’s Corporate Crime Circle in Islamabad.

The arrests followed raids conducted by a joint team of the FIA and the Human Organ Transplant Authority at a residence in Sector F-7/1 and a location in Sector E-11 in Islamabad. Authorities recovered approximately 400 to 500 kilograms of fresh and dried human placentas from refrigerators at the sites. An additional export shipment weighing 580kg, misdeclared as sheep placenta and destined for Hanoi, Vietnam, was intercepted at Islamabad International Airport. In total, authorities recovered 1,241kg of human placentas linked to the network.

Deputy Attorney General Raja Shafqat Abbasi stated that the case was registered under the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 2010, along with provisions of the Pakistan Penal Code, following a complaint by HOTA medical officer Hina Kanwal. Investigators revealed the placentas were procured via a Punjab-based waste management company employee and allegedly processed for commercial export to produce anti-ageing injections. While prosecutors argued that placentas constitute human organs carrying up to 10 years of imprisonment and are a flight risk, the court observed that waste material warrants further inquiry.

This legal development matters as it addresses an underground transnational network allegedly exploiting medical waste for commercial and cosmetic gains. The illicit trade has raised serious public health concerns regarding the disposal of infectious medical waste from hospitals. Further investigations remain underway to uncover financial trails, export chains, and potential complicity of officials from customs and other departments.

stories.title: راولپنڈی: مری روڈ پر حادثے سے بچنے والا شہری نالہ لئی میں گر کر ہلاک
stories.summary:
راولپنڈی کے مصروف علاقے مری روڈ پر ایک دردناک حادثے میں بچ جانے والا معمر شہری اچانک نالہ لئی میں گر کر جاں بحق ہو گیا۔ یہ واقعہ مریڑ چوک کے قریب پیش آیا جہاں بزرگ شخص کو پہلے ہی ایک ٹریفک حادثے کا سامنا کرنا پڑا تھا، جس کے بعد راہگیروں نے اسے اٹھا کر سڑک کے کنارے بٹھا دیا تھا۔

حکام کے مطابق ابتدائی حادثے کے بعد وہ بزرگ شہری اچانک پل کے کنارے سے نیچے نالہ لئی میں جا گرا۔ حادثے کی اطلاع ملتے ہی ریسکیو ٹیمیں فوری طور پر موقع پر روانہ ہوئیں، تاہم وہ بروقت پہنچنے کے باوجود شہری کی جان نہیں بچا سکیں اور وہ پانی میں گر کر دم توڑ چکا تھا۔

ریسکیو حکام نے موقع پر پہنچ کر لاش کو نالہ لئی سے باہر نکالا۔ اس ناگہانی واقعے کے بعد علاقے میں غم و فضا پھیل گئی اور شہری انتظامیہ کے حفاظتی انتظامات پر بھی سوالات اٹھائے جانے لگے۔

اس حادثے سے متعلق قانونی کارروائی اور ضابطے کی کارروائیوں کے لیے مقامی حکام نے متعلقہ امور کی جانچ پڑتال شروع کر دی ہے تاکہ تمام حقائق کا تعین کیا جا سکے اور ضروری کارروائی عمل میں لائی جا سکے۔

stories.title: عمران خان کا اعلیٰ عدلیہ کے سربراہان کو خط، صحت سے متعلق شدید خدشات کا اظہار
stories.summary:
پاکستان تحریک انصاف کے بانی عمران خان نے چیف جسٹس آف پاکستان، چیف جسٹس وفاقی آئینی عدالت اور چیف جسٹس اسلام آباد ہائی کورٹ کے نام ایک تحریری خط ارسال کیا ہے۔ بیرسٹر سلمان صفدر کے توسط سے پہنچائے جانے والے اس خط میں بانی پی ٹی آئی نے اپنی بگڑتی ہوئی صحت پر گہرے خدشات کا اظہار کرتے ہوئے موقف اختیار کیا ہے کہ ڈاکٹروں نے انہیں برین ہیمرج اور دل کا دورہ پڑنے کے خطرے سے خبردار کیا ہے کیونکہ ان کا بلڈ پریشر 193 تک جاپہنچا ہے۔ انہوں نے استدعا کی ہے کہ عدالتی فیصلوں پر حقیقی عمل درآمد یقینی بنایا جائے کیونکہ زندہ رہنے کی صورت میں ہی وہ اپنی بے گناہی ثابت کر سکیں گے۔

دوسری جانب بانی پی ٹی آئی کی اہلیہ بشریٰ بی بی نے بھی اپنے علاج اور سرجری کے لیے اسلام آباد ہائی کورٹ میں دائر درخواست کے ذریعے رجوع کیا ہے۔ لطیف کھوسہ اور بیرسٹر سلمان صفدر کے توسط سے دائر کی گئی اس درخواست میں مؤقف اپنایا گیا ہے کہ بشریٰ بی بی کو دیکھنے میں شدید مشکلات اور آنکھ میں تکلیف کا سامنا ہے، اور 10 نومبر کو ملاقات کے دوران بانی پی ٹی آئی نے بشریٰ بی بی کی صحت کی سنگینی سے آگاہ کیا تھا۔ عدالت سے استدعا کی گئی ہے کہ ان کا مکمل طبی ریکارڈ طلب کیا جائے اور فوری طبی نگہداشت کے لیے انہیں کسی خصوصی اسپتال منتقل کرنے کے انتظامات کیے جائیں۔

مذکورہ قانونی چارہ جوئی کے دوران یہ تفصیلات بھی سامنے آئیں کہ جیل میں طبی معائنے کے بعد ڈاکٹروں نے بشریٰ بی بی کی آنکھ کی سرجری کی ضرورت ظاہر کی تھی۔ درخواست میں اس بات پر زور دیا گیا ہے کہ قیدیوں کی صحت اور طبی سہولتوں کی فراہمی پر کسی قسم کا سمجھوتہ نہیں کیا جانا چاہیے اور فوری طور پر تمام ضروری طبی امداد فراہم کی جائے۔

یہ پیشرفت ایسے وقت میں سامنے آئی ہے جب ملک بھر میں سیاسی اور عدلیہ کی سطح پر مختلف قانونی امور زیر بحث ہیں، اور پی ٹی آئی قیادت کی جانب سے جیل میں موجود رہنماؤں کی صحت اور سکیورٹی کو لے کر مسلسل تشویش کا اظہار کیا جا رہا ہے۔ عدالتوں کی جانب سے ان درخواستوں پر آئندہ سماعتوں میں مزید احکامات متوقع ہیں۔

stories.title: Finance Minister Aurangzeb Urges Banks to Increase Priority Sector Lending
stories.summary:
Pakistan's Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb has called upon commercial banks, including Habib Bank Limited, to expand financing for critical economic sectors. The appeal was made during a meeting in Islamabad with an HBL delegation headed by President and CEO Muhammad Nassir Salim. Discussions focused on the banking sector's vital contribution to driving economic growth, boosting investments, and widening financial inclusion across the country.

During the talks, Aurangzeb emphasized the necessity of directing funds toward priority areas such as small and medium enterprises, agriculture, housing, and electric vehicles under the Pakistan Accelerated Vehicle Electrification Scheme. He noted that robust financial institutions are essential for facilitating business transactions and providing enterprises and individuals with necessary services. The delegation also presented updates on HBL's international outreach, engagement with overseas markets, and the positive response to the Roshan Digital Account 2.0 initiative.

Furthermore, both parties explored avenues to channel long-term capital into viable infrastructure projects through enhanced private sector participation. They discussed strengthening government-HBL cooperation to position Pakistan as an appealing destination for foreign and domestic investors. Aurangzeb stressed that close coordination between state officials and banking leaders is imperative for addressing emerging economic hurdles and fostering an enabling environment for private-led growth.

This engagement is significant for shaping Pakistan's broader economic strategy and stabilizing domestic financial markets. By directing liquidity toward productive sectors, the government hopes to stimulate long-term development and improve the overall business climate. Continued collaboration between financial institutions and policymakers aims to tackle structural challenges and support sustainable economic recovery.

stories.title: Chaudhry Salik Hussain Refuses Apology or Damages in Maryam Nawaz Defamation Suit
stories.summary:
Federal Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain has formally rejected demands to apologize or pay financial damages in a defamation case filed by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz. Details of the minister's official response emerged through ARY News on Monday. The legal dispute stems from earlier corruption allegations made by Salik regarding the Punjab administration, which prompted Maryam Nawaz to issue a legal notice demanding Rs5 billion in compensation.

In his written reply, Chaudhry Salik maintained that his remarks did not provide any valid grounds for a defamation claim. He argued that his statements had been misquoted in the legal notice and categorically refused to retract his words, issue an apology, or offer monetary compensation. Furthermore, the federal minister stated his intention to present evidence of corruption before the appropriate legal and judicial forums in the future.

Salik also contended that public statements made by Maryam Nawaz herself in Jhelum validated the concerns he had initially raised regarding corruption. Additionally, he accused the Punjab chief minister of misusing public resources and the Advocate General's Office for personal legal matters. He asserted that taxpayer-funded government legal resources should not be exploited to handle private disputes.

This high-profile political clash highlights ongoing tensions between federal figures and provincial leadership in Pakistan. The case underscores broader debates surrounding the use of public resources for personal defamation litigation and the limits of political speech. As the matter proceeds, public attention remains focused on whether concrete evidence of corruption will be formally submitted to legal authorities.

stories.title: PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Expresses Disappointment Over Federal Constitutional Court Order
stories.summary:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan has voiced disappointment regarding the Federal Constitutional Court's amended order concerning detained party workers. Speaking to reporters outside the FCC in Islamabad alongside Sardar Latif Khosa and members of the Insaf Lawyers Forum, Gohar stated that the revised ruling failed to deliver the relief sought for thousands of incarcerated activists.

PTI had approached the court to allow the Peshawar High Court to review pending petitions and determine their maintainability and jurisdiction. Gohar stressed that thousands of party supporters remain detained in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance. He argued that denying individuals access to a judicial forum and keeping them imprisoned violates their fundamental right to a proper legal hearing and an effective defense against state detention.

The FCC issued an amended order allowing the PHC to hear regular petitions filed under Article 199 of the Constitution. However, the constitutional court maintained restrictions specifically prohibiting the PHC from handling matters related to Governor's Rule and MPO detentions in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. This revision modifies the court's earlier November 5 restraining order, which had suspended all PHC proceedings under Article 199.

This legal standoff carries significant weight for Pakistan's political landscape, directly affecting the detained opposition members and the jurisdictional boundaries of provincial high courts. Barrister Gohar urged the FCC to expedite hearings on these liberty matters to ensure justice is served. The ongoing friction highlights the complex legal battles between political entities and judicial bodies in the country.

stories.title: Teenager Mirra Andreeva Claims WTA Finals Title Without Dropping a Set
stories.summary:
Nineteen-year-old Mirra Andreeva triumphed at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells on Sunday, defeating Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3. The Russian teenager completed a flawless tournament debut by winning all five of her matches without losing a single set. During the final, Andreeva secured a tightly contested opening set lasting 55 minutes, and despite a lengthy seventh game in the second set, she maintained her momentum to seal the victory when Svitolina hit an overhead into the net.

With this victory, the French Open champion collects the maximum prize money of $3.37 million, receives the Billie Jean King Trophy, and claims a custom purple Mercedes-Benz AMG SL 55. Because she does not yet possess a driver's licence, Andreeva joked about driving it a few metres or remaining a passenger. The win also lifts her to a career-high world ranking of number two, placing her within 300 points of Elena Rybakina.

Elina Svitolina, the 2018 champion, expressed hope that her strong form and return to elite competition following motherhood would inspire other women and athletes. Maintaining her established policy regarding Russian and Belarusian competitors following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Svitolina did not shake hands with Andreeva after the match or acknowledge her during the trophy ceremony. Svitolina also thanked supporters in Ukraine for backing her journey.

In the doubles final of the tournament, Czech player Katerina Siniakova and American Taylor Townsend defeated the Italian pair Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini. The eight-day, $10 million season-ending event took place at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden after being relocated from Riyadh due to the US-Israeli war on Iran. Organizers announced that the tournament will shift to Charlotte, North Carolina, next year.

stories.title: Four nations urge Israel to provide rapid humanitarian aid to Gaza
stories.summary:
Australia, Britain, Canada, and Italy jointly urged the Israeli government on Sunday to grant immediate, rapid, and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza, describing the current humanitarian conditions as dire. The foreign ministries of the four nations emphasized that recent heavy rains and flooding have severely worsened the suffering of displaced residents.

According to Hamas-led authorities in Gaza, practically the entire population has been displaced at least once, and severe storms earlier in the month washed away tens of thousands of tents. The joint statement highlighted that approximately 150,000 tents and other essential survival supplies are currently being held at the border, blocked from entering the territory.

The coalition stressed that the crisis remains entirely reversible if authorities act immediately before the full onset of winter. This appeal follows a similar international warning issued by the European Union on Saturday regarding the escalating humanitarian emergency in Gaza.

stories.title: Governors Awards honor Glenn Close and Ridley Scott with Oscars
stories.summary:
Hollywood's annual Governors Awards celebrated the enduring careers of actor Glenn Close and director Ridley Scott on Sunday, bestowing them with honorary Oscars at a star-studded gala in Los Angeles. The event served as one of the initial red-carpet gatherings of the movie awards season, drawing numerous industry heavyweights and A-list actors.

Glenn Close, 79, has received eight Academy Award nominations throughout her career for roles in films such as “Fatal Attraction” and “The Big Chill,” but has never won a competitive Oscar. Introduced by her “Dangerous Liaisons” co-star John Malkovich, Close reflected that simply being in the room among peers who continuously challenge and inspire her was the greatest honor. Ridley Scott, an 88-year-old director with four Oscar nominations for acclaimed works like “Alien,” “Blade Runner,” and “Gladiator,” accepted his award via video. Introduced by actor Matt Damon, Scott paid tribute to his late brother, director Tony Scott.

The gala also honored Disney animator Floyd Norman alongside producers Pamela Koffler and Christine Vachon. The recipients were selected by the board of governors of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

stories.title: Lawyers submit affidavits detailing jail meeting with Imran and Bushra
stories.summary:
Legal counsel representing former prime minister Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, have submitted affidavits to the Islamabad High Court (IHC) detailing a three-hour meeting held with the incarcerated couple at Adiala jail on November 11. Concurrently, Bushra filed a fresh criminal miscellaneous application under Section 561-A seeking her complete medical records and an immediate transfer to a specialized hospital, citing deteriorating eyesight and unhygienic prison conditions.

The affidavits, submitted by Senior Advocate Sardar Muhammad Latif Khosa and Barrister Salman Safdar, followed an IHC order directing authorities to facilitate the legal consultation. During the meeting, Imran provided instructions regarding his ongoing legal cases and health, while the discussion largely centered on Bushra's medical complications. Bushra stated she was diagnosed with a mature cataract and faced another major surgery scheduled around November 15. She reported severely impaired vision in both eyes, persistent pain requiring daily medication, and cautioned that attending doctors warned of potential permanent blindness if post-surgical infections occurred.

Furthermore, the legal team brought court attention to poor sanitary conditions in Bushra's confinement area, noting complaints of frequent insect bites, skin rashes, and the presence of rodents, insects, and small snakes inside the room. The application also pointed out that the prison's duty medical officer is a gynaecologist rather than an ophthalmologist.

In her newly filed application concerning her appeal in the £190 million Al-Qadir Trust case, Bushra requested the court to incorporate these latest disclosures and direct respondents, including the Adiala jail superintendent and the NAB chairman, to produce her comprehensive medical files and ensure necessary surgical treatment.

stories.title: Islamabad Court Grants Police Four-Day Physical Remand of Two Murder Suspects
stories.summary:
A judicial magistrate in Islamabad has granted a four-day physical remand for two suspects, a woman and a seminary teacher, arrested in connection with the tragic death of a 13-year-old girl. The victim, who was a seminary student, had been living with close relatives at the Police Lines Headquarters in Islamabad's sector H-11 and was allegedly subjected to violence at the residence of a Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) director.

The suspects were brought before Judicial Magistrate Naima Iffat at the district and sessions court by police officials who had initially requested an eight-day physical remand. The investigating officer told the court that the extended custody was necessary for further interrogation and to advance the ongoing inquiry. Following a brief reservation of its decision, the court ultimately approved a four-day remand.

The arrests followed the filing of a first information report at the Shams Colony police station under Section 302 for intentional murder, initiated by the victim's father. The complainant, a resident of Rahim Yar Khan, stated he was informed that his daughter had suddenly fallen ill before passing away at a hospital. The father subsequently requested a thorough police investigation and legal action after noticing visible signs of torture on his daughter's body.

This legal development unfolds amidst a backdrop of various national events and administrative reports in Pakistan, ranging from political discussions and climate delegation nominations to legal proceedings and upcoming local government considerations. The case highlights ongoing concerns regarding domestic violence and accountability within institutional residences, as local authorities continue their detailed examination of the circumstances surrounding the young girl's death.

stories.title: Alexander Zverev and Ben Shelton Secure Opening Victories at ATP Finals
stories.summary:
World number one Alexander Zverev began his ATP Finals campaign in Turin with a solid 6-4, 6-4 victory over 20-year-old Spanish debutant Rafael Jodar. Needing just one hour and 27 minutes to dispatch the tournament's breakout star, Zverev utilized ten aces and a strong return of serve to overcome the world number 11. Despite enduring a difficult autumn marked by mental and physical exhaustion and a first-match exit at the Paris Masters, the German player expressed satisfaction with his performance, though acknowledging room for improvement.

In the evening fixture within the John McEnroe group, American third seed Ben Shelton earned his first-ever victory at the season-ending tournament by defeating France's seventh-seeded Arthur Fils 6-2, 3-6, 6-3. Shelton dominated the opening set before Fils, the first Frenchman to qualify for the event in a decade, adapted by extending rallies and claiming the second set. The final set proved intensely physical, with Shelton successfully fighting off break points using powerful aces and forehands to secure the hard-fought win and early momentum in the round-robin stage.

The tournament features an elite field of eight players, though the dynamics of the competition are influenced by other top-tier athletes. Zverev claimed the world number one ranking in early November after securing his first two Grand Slam titles in 2026, yet Spain's Carlos Alcaraz enters as a strong favorite following a successful comeback from a wrist injury. Meanwhile, two-time defending champion Jannik Sinner remains absent from the event due to a knee injury sustained after his Wimbledon victory in July.

The opening day results set a competitive tone for the remainder of the week-long championship in Italy. Both Zverev and Shelton look to build upon their early successes as they navigate the demanding round-robin matches against the world's finest tennis professionals.

stories.title: Zverev Wins Opener as Four Nations Urge Immediate Gaza Humanitarian Access
stories.summary:
World number one Alexander Zverev cruised through his opening match at the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin on Sunday, defeating Spanish debutant Rafael Jodar 6-4, 6-4. Zverev, who previously won the tournament in 2018 and 2021, needed just one hour and 27 minutes to overcome the 20-year-old Spanish player. Despite suffering from physical and mental exhaustion earlier in the autumn and a quick exit at the Paris Masters, Zverev relied on ten aces and a powerful return of serve to stifle his opponent, breaking Jodar in the seventh game of the first set and the third game of the second set.

In the same group, American third seed Ben Shelton secured his first-ever victory at the tournament by defeating France's Arthur Fils 6-2, 3-6, 6-3. Shelton overpowered Fils in the opening set, but the 22-year-old Frenchman fought back to level the match before Shelton utilized crucial aces and heavy forehands in the final set to seal the win. In broader tennis context, Zverev achieved the world number one ranking in November following two Grand Slam titles in 2026, while competitors like Carlos Alcaraz enter as favorites and Jannik Sinner remains sidelined by a knee injury.

Meanwhile, in international diplomacy, representatives from Australia, Britain, Canada, and Italy issued a joint statement on Sunday urging the Israeli government to permit rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza. Describing the ground situation as dire, the four nations called for an immediate halt to ongoing delays in aid delivery to alleviate civilian suffering in the region.

The combined updates reflect a mix of high-level athletic competition in Italy and pressing geopolitical appeals concerning humanitarian aid in the Middle East. Authorities and sports figures alike remain focused on their respective objectives as these international stories unfold.

stories.title: England Coach Tuchel Hails Statement Victory Over World Champions Spain
stories.summary:
England secured a memorable 3-2 victory over world champions Spain in the Nations League on Sunday, a result manager Thomas Tuchel described as a definitive statement. Playing away at the Metropolitano stadium in Madrid, the visitors surged to a commanding three-goal lead through successful efforts from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa, and Ben White. The performance marked a high point in Tuchel's tenure, showcasing the squad's unity, quality, and tactical execution against top-tier opposition.

The momentum of the match shifted dramatically when English midfielder Elliot Anderson was shown a red card, leaving his team with 10 players for the final half-hour. Capitalizing on the numerical advantage, Spain mounted a comeback as Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams scored two goals to narrow the deficit. Despite enduring intense pressure during the closing stages, England successfully defended their lead to withstand the reigning world champions.

The defeat brought an abrupt end to Spain's remarkable unbeaten streak of 44 competitive matches, marking their first competitive loss since March 2023. Tuchel praised his squad for their confidence and resilience under extreme pressure, noting that the difficult final thirty minutes felt significantly longer given the quality of the Spanish side. The German coach emphasized that the team has made substantial progress since their previous challenges following the World Cup.

Ultimately, the hard-fought triumph serves as a major milestone for England's current campaign under Tuchel. By overcoming the numerical disadvantage and defeating a historic opponent on foreign soil, the team validated their competitive growth and ability to perform at the highest international level.

stories.title: Japan Records Zero Economic Growth in Third Quarter Amid Iran War Impact
stories.summary:
Japan experienced stagnant economic growth during the third quarter, registering gross domestic product at zero percent, according to official data released on Monday by the cabinet office. This performance fell short of market expectations, which had anticipated a growth rate of 0.1 percent. Additionally, on an annualised basis, the economy contracted by 0.1 percent for the July through September period, contrasting with market predictions of a 0.2 percent expansion.

The underwhelming economic results were primarily driven by the ongoing, lingering effects of the Iran war, which continued to weigh heavily on performance. Despite this stagnation, inflationary pressures are actively building within the country. As a result, the Bank of Japan remains widely anticipated to implement another interest rate hike in December.

Analyst Marcel Thieliant from Capital Economics stated that Monday's disappointing economic reading is unlikely to deter the central bank from moving forward with its plans. Thieliant further noted that the central bank may ultimately need to tighten monetary policy much more aggressively than previously anticipated because inflation is poised to surge significantly.

This unexpected economic standstill highlights the vulnerability of Japan's recovery to external geopolitical shocks, particularly conflicts affecting global stability and resources. Understanding these domestic and international pressures is crucial for assessing future monetary policies, consumer costs, and the overall trajectory of the world's fourth-largest economy as it navigates these growing economic hurdles.

stories.title: Ousted Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina Vows to Return in December
stories.summary:
Ousted Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina announced her intention to return home in December despite facing a death sentence and numerous other legal challenges. Hasina was previously sentenced to death in absentia after a Bangladeshi court convicted her of crimes against humanity following a deadly crackdown on protesters. Her 15-year iron-fisted rule ended in August 2024 due to a student-led uprising, forcing her to flee into hiding in India, where she has remained ever since.

Speaking to AFP via an email interview, the 79-year-old former leader acknowledged the severe dangers awaiting her. Bangladeshi authorities recently stated that she has no remaining legal recourse after missing appeal deadlines and will face immediate execution upon return. Dhaka has requested her extradition from India, a matter currently under legal review. Hasina, however, dismissed the legitimacy of her trial and criticized contradictory statements from officials, asserting she aims to return voluntarily rather than seeking Indian assistance.

Analysts believe her return pledge is a strategy to maintain political relevance, sustain support, and keep her banned Awami League party alive. Beyond the capital punishment ruling, Hasina faces more than 600 additional allegations, including corruption charges, which she dismissed as false. Her legal team has applied for a passport and national identity card through the New Delhi high commission in preparation for the journey.

Hasina denied any involvement of her party in recent petrol bomb attacks in Bangladesh. Emphasizing her readiness to face the consequences, she stated that while she wishes to live and serve her country, she is fully prepared to confront death as the ultimate price for returning home to Bangladesh.

stories.title: UN Climate Chief Warns of AI's Dual Nature at COP31 Talks
stories.summary:
Artificial intelligence presents both immense potential and severe peril for global climate efforts, United Nations climate chief Simon Stiell stated on Monday. Speaking at COP31 in the Mediterranean city of Antalya, Stiell addressed the launch of the voluntary Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge, introduced by host country Turkiye. The initiative aims to leverage technology for climate solutions while evaluating its expanding environmental risks.

Stiell emphasized that frontier technologies act as a double-edged sword, warning that the heavy energy and water consumption of AI data centres has driven up community power bills and carbon footprints. He stressed that the benefits of artificial intelligence must outweigh its growing costs and urged corporate leaders to align their business plans with international climate goals by powering data centres with renewable energy sources.

During the panel, Turkey's Industry and Technology Minister Mehmet Fatih Kacir announced that the Antalya AI Pledge had secured 80 endorsements, though he did not clarify the exact breakdown between countries and corporate entities. Kacir highlighted the necessity of simultaneously reducing the environmental footprint of AI and utilizing its capabilities to modernize industries and accelerate green development.

The discussions at COP31 underline the critical intersection between rapid technological advancement and global environmental policy. As artificial intelligence continues to expand across various sectors, addressing its resource demands remains a pressing challenge for world leaders, policymakers, and corporate executives striving to meet agreed climate objectives.

stories.title: Sudanese Army Drone Strike Kills 15 Civilians in West Kordofan
stories.summary:
A Sudanese army drone strike in West Kordofan resulted in the deaths of 15 people, including four children who were playing football at the time. The attack struck the village of Abu Qalb on Sunday, utilizing a double-tap method that also destroyed several homes and injured other residents in the area, according to local sources and monitoring groups.

A survivor of the attack, who requested anonymity for safety reasons, shared the personal tragedy of the incident. He reported losing nine of his own relatives in the bombardment, noting that two of the young victims had already lost their father earlier in the ongoing conflict.

The death toll and details of the devastation were independently confirmed by the Kordofan Observatory, a local rights monitor. The organization verified that the Sunday strike not only claimed numerous lives but also burned down a significant number of residential buildings in the village.

This deadly incident adds to the mounting civilian casualties in the region's protracted conflict. It highlights the severe ongoing dangers faced by non-combatants, particularly children, as military operations continue to impact civilian infrastructure and communities across Sudan.

stories.title: US Expert Urges Pakistani Startups to Prioritize Revenue Over Funding
stories.summary:
US venture-building professional David D’Angelo has advised Pakistani startups to prioritize customer acquisition and revenue generation rather than making venture capital fundraising their main objective. Speaking exclusively to Business Recorder Research, D’Angelo noted that this obsession reflects a broader startup culture influenced by Silicon Valley. He recommended that founders explore alternative financing models like bootstrapping, arguing that building a repeatable sales model naturally attracts investment.

D’Angelo brings significant experience, having worked with hundreds of university-backed hard-tech startups tied to institutions such as MIT, Stanford, Princeton, Northwestern, and Johns Hopkins, helping founders secure more than $600 million in follow-up funding. He cautioned Pakistani entrepreneurs against competing internationally strictly on low prices, explaining that cheap pricing damages perceptions of product quality. Instead, he advised founders to price based on the value in the target buyer's market rather than local cost bases.

Furthermore, D’Angelo pointed out common mistakes made by emerging-market startups targeting international clients, including poor market positioning, lack of credibility, excessive reliance on cold outreach, and slow communication. He emphasized that US business deals fail more frequently due to slow replies than inferior products, urging founders to answer during US business hours. To alter international investor perceptions, he stated that local startups must hit meaningful financial milestones, such as achieving over $10 million in annual recurring revenue.

Finally, D’Angelo called for government-backed grants to support Pakistan's capital-intensive deep-tech startups, noting that non-dilutive funding is vital for technology development and commercialization before revenue materializes. He argued that institutional grants combined with a willing venture capital ecosystem could successfully foster high-risk sectors like medtech, agtech, and cleantech across Pakistan.

stories.title: DRAP Issues Safety Alert Regarding Falsified Children's Vaccine Vial
stories.summary:
The Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) has issued an official warning concerning the sale and distribution of a falsified version of the Hexaxim vaccine. This vaccine is typically administered to infants and young children to provide protection against six major infectious diseases, including diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, hepatitis B, polio, and Haemophilus influenzae type b infections.

According to the regulatory alert, Hoechst Pakistan Limited—the Karachi-based local distributor for Sanofi—notified DRAP that Hexaxim vaccine batches carrying batch number X3H421VA in vial form are completely unauthorized for import into Pakistan. The company clarified that the legitimate Hexaxim vaccine is only registered within the country as a pre-filled syringe rather than a liquid vial presentation.

DRAP warned that utilizing this fraudulent vial version presents severe health hazards, potentially leading to therapeutic failure or dangerous adverse reactions. In response to the threat, the authority directed its Regulatory Field Force alongside provincial drug control departments to survey supply chains actively and seize any counterfeit products found in the market.

Consumers have been strongly advised to avoid purchasing or using the identified vaccine product. DRAP urged anyone who has already administered the item and suffered health complications to contact a physician immediately and report the occurrence to the National Pharmacovigilance Centre, while strictly sourcing therapeutics through authorized pharmacies.

stories.title: ECO Meeting in Islamabad Focuses on Regional Energy and Cooperation
stories.summary:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called for the creation of a reliable and sustainable regional energy mechanism during his address at the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers in Islamabad. Speaking on Monday, Araghchi highlighted how the US-Israeli war on Iran has severely restricted crucial fuel supply routes like the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab. He emphasized that the region requires an independent security framework and sustainable energy mechanisms to protect energy flows and mitigate external geopolitical shocks.

Addressing broader regional cooperation, Araghchi noted that the ECO is evolving into an active platform for collective action and joint efforts. He stressed the importance of adopting a modern, inclusive trade agreement and stated that Iran remains committed to diplomatic solutions despite facing Western aggression, economic coercion, and blockades. He also stated that regional territories and airspaces must not serve as launching pads for attacks, and characterized Iran's defensive measures as strictly targeted at aggressor military bases. Additionally, he condemned the ongoing destruction and humanitarian crisis caused by Israeli forces in Palestine.

Pakistan is hosting the high-level meeting under the chairmanship for 2026-27, themed 'Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO'. In his opening address, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar outlined five major priorities: expanding trade, improving regional connectivity, advancing the ECO Trade Agreement, building disaster resilience, and promoting human development. Dar underscored that regional connectivity depends heavily on mutual trust, adherence to international law, and predictable transit arrangements.

Furthermore, Dar addressed the situation in Afghanistan, stating that Pakistan desires a stable and peaceful neighbor, but emphasized that Afghan authorities must actively address regional security concerns and the threat of terrorism. He asserted that a secure environment and integrated economic partnerships are vital for unlocking the full natural resource and transport potential across Central Asia, South Asia, and the Arabian Sea ports.

stories.title: Spain Coach Remains Optimistic After Defeat Against England
stories.summary:
Spain manager Luis de la Fuente expressed strong optimism following his team's 3-2 Nations League defeat against England, stating that his squad would return with renewed energy. The loss concluded an impressive 44-match unbeaten run that dated back to March 2023, a historic stretch during which La Roja captured both the Euro 2024 and 2026 World Cup titles to dominate international football.

Reflecting on the setback in his post-match comments to reporters, De la Fuente viewed the outcome as the beginning of a fresh challenge. He emphasized his desire to restart a winning trajectory similar to their previous streak. Spain had already secured qualification for the upcoming Nations League quarter-finals scheduled to take place next year.

The manager noted that the defeat serves to ground the team and highlights the immense difficulty of maintaining such a long period of elite success. He acknowledged that opponents constantly view beating Spain as a major goal, which he considers a positive indicator of their status.

While admitting that the unfamiliar taste of defeat brings temporary disappointment, De la Fuente affirmed that the squad's ambition remains intact. He confirmed that Spain will focus heavily in March on navigating the knockout rounds and making another deep run toward winning the Nations League finals.

stories.title: Malaysian Palm Oil Futures Open Lower Following Declines in Competing Oils
stories.summary:
Malaysian palm oil futures experienced a downward start on Monday, interrupting a three-session winning streak. The market downturn was primarily driven by falling prices in rival edible oils and crude oil.

Specifically, the benchmark palm oil contract scheduled for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange dropped by 37 ringgit, representing a 0.81% decline. This brought the trading price down to 4,528 ringgit, which is equivalent to $1,108, per metric ton during early trading hours.

The drop highlights the interconnected nature of global commodity markets, where fluctuations in alternative vegetable oils and petroleum products immediately impact palm oil valuations. Traders and analysts monitor these external energy and agricultural sectors closely to gauge daily market direction in Kuala Lumpur.

Such shifts matter to producers and international buyers alike, as they influence export costs and agricultural revenue for the region. The reversal illustrates how quickly market sentiment can pivot in response to broader commodity trends.

stories.title: Pakistani Prime Minister Criticizes Delays in Foreign-Funded Development Projects
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has raised serious concerns regarding persistent and unnecessary delays affecting foreign-assisted development projects in Pakistan. According to media reports citing official sources, he has ordered the immediate creation of special working groups to tackle these ongoing administrative bottlenecks.

A comprehensive report delivered to the prime minister revealed a troubling decade-long trend showing that not a single foreign-funded development initiative was completed on schedule over the past ten years. These prolonged setbacks have forced the nation to continuously pay additional commitment charges amounting to 0.25 percent annually throughout the decade, creating financial burdens that the prime minister intends to eliminate.

The assessment identified legal complexities surrounding land acquisition as the primary driver behind the sluggish implementation. Furthermore, international financing institutions such as the Asian Development Bank and the World Bank expressed strong reservations regarding the frequent replacement of project directors, with certain initiatives seeing as many as four different directors in a single year without prior consultation with global lenders.

Additional operational hurdles involve delayed recruitment of critical staff, particularly within the infrastructure sector where execution challenges remain severe. Concurrently, international pressure continues to mount as officials from Australia, Britain, Canada, and Italy issued a joint appeal urging the Israeli government to lift delivery restrictions and grant rapid, unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza due to dire conditions on the ground.

stories.title: Tokyo Stocks Drop Sharply as Tech and Chip Shares Lead Market Decline
stories.summary:
Japan's Nikkei share average experienced a steep decline on Monday, falling 1.6% to reach 60,182.50 by the midday recess. The downturn was heavily influenced by losses in heavyweight chip-related stocks as investors reacted to turbulence surrounding artificial intelligence giant Nvidia ahead of its scheduled earnings report on Tuesday.

The market was also processing wariness regarding upcoming artificial intelligence benchmarks, including the highly anticipated initial public offering of Claude chatbot creator Anthropic, which is expected to price on Wednesday with trading to begin the following day. Prominent Nvidia suppliers suffered major drops, with Advantest plummeting 9.9% and Tokyo Electron sliding 5.2%. Together, these two chip equipment makers accounted for 904 points of the broader index's net 960-point loss.

Despite the index-level drop, winners actually outnumbered losers among the Nikkei's 225 components, with 115 stocks rising, 108 falling, and two remaining flat. Broader measures like the Topix recorded shallower losses by easing 0.4%, while sectors such as financials and retailers outperformed the market. Credit card provider Credit Saison surged nearly 17% following an upgraded earnings forecast, and furniture seller Nitori gained 7.8% on its results.

Investor caution intensified following reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday amid revelations of extramarital affairs, plunging the chipmaker into crisis. Media sources indicate that Huang has discussed a potential return with confidants, even as the company approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas for the position. Across the Tokyo Stock Exchange, AI-exposed sectors performed worst, with nonferrous metals dropping 5.8% and electrical appliances sliding 3%.

stories.title: Pakistan Deputy Prime Minister Stresses Afghan Security Measures for Economic Progress
stories.summary:
Addressing the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers in Islamabad, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar emphasized that regional cooperation depends heavily on Afghanistan addressing legitimate security concerns. He stated that meaningful progress requires Afghan authorities to tackle the threat of terrorism directed at neighbouring countries.

Dar outlined Pakistan's desire for a peaceful, stable, and prosperous Afghanistan that integrates fully into regional frameworks. He noted that a secure environment is essential for sustained economic partnerships, transport connectivity, and trust between states, warning that unresolved disputes and ignored international commitments undermine economic growth. Pakistan advocates for peaceful dispute resolution through dialogue, diplomacy, and adherence to international law and the United Nations Charter.

Highlighting regional integration, Dar urged ECO member states to leverage geographic proximity to enhance transport corridors, streamline border procedures, and improve trade frameworks. He mentioned that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, and the Foreign Office remain actively engaged with international partners to foster regional stability and de-escalation.

As the current ECO chair, Pakistan plans to prioritize expanded market access, stronger regional value chains, and increased private-sector participation, especially among small and medium-sized enterprises. Dar concluded by reaffirming Pakistan's dedication to the ECO Charter, calling for continued collaboration in climate resilience, human development, and trade connectivity from Central Asia to South Asia and Pakistani seaports.

stories.title: Australian and New Zealand Currencies Plummet Amid Surging U.S. Yields
stories.summary:
The Australian and New Zealand dollars tumbled to multi-month lows as rising United States Treasury yields and a strong dollar erased their historical yield advantages. In Sydney trade on Monday, the Australian dollar dropped 0.2 percent to 0.6759 US dollars, reaching its lowest point since late January following a 1.2 percent decline the previous week. Meanwhile, the New Zealand dollar slipped 0.1 percent to hit a 19-month low of 0.5520 US dollars. Both currencies suffered as markets anticipated aggressive interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve to combat inflation, while local yields failed to keep pace.

The shifting monetary policy expectations have nearly wiped out the local yield advantages that previously supported both Oceanian currencies. The yield spread between Australian 10-year government bonds and US Treasuries shrank to zero from 80 basis points in March. New Zealand's previous premium swung into a negative 27 basis points compared to a positive 60 basis points previously. ANZ strategist David Croy noted that the low interest rate environment makes holding the New Zealand dollar costly from a carry perspective, with relative interest rates unlikely to favor the currency anytime soon.

Adding to the downward pressure, the Australian dollar fell nearly 3 percent against its New Zealand counterpart from recent peaks as financial markets shifted from pricing in further rate hikes by the Reserve Bank of Australia to anticipating cuts next year. Commonwealth Bank of Australia analysts expect the Australian currency to consolidate around 68 cents, though upcoming domestic jobs data could offer support. The Reserve Bank of Australia delivered its fifth rate hike of the year earlier this month, lifting its cash rate to an 18-year high of 4.85 percent, and will publish its November meeting minutes on Tuesday.

Global market turbulence and weak equity markets have further compounded the pressure on both currencies, with upcoming Nvidia earnings and Anthropic's initial public offering expected to test investor sentiment. Analysts warn that the Australian dollar faces mounting risks and could finish the year below out-of-consensus forecasts of 0.68 US dollars, as the general path of least resistance for the exchange rate remains downward over the coming months.

stories.title: اسلام آباد میں 13 سالہ گھریلو ملازمہ کی ہلاکت پر مقدمہ درج، دو گرفتار
stories.summary:
اسلام آباد کے سرکاری رہائشی علاقے میں ایک پولیس افسر کے گھر کام کرنے والی تیرہ سالہ گھریلو ملازمہ فاطمہ کی پراسرار حالات میں ہلاکت کے بعد پولیس نے قتل کی دفعات کے تحت مقدمہ درج کر لیا ہے۔ واقعہ اتوار کے روز پیش آیا تھا جس کے بعد بچی کے ورثا اور عوامی حلقوں کی جانب سے شدید تحفظات کا اظہار کیا گیا تھا۔ بچی کو تشویشناک حالت میں قائداعظم ہسپتال منتقل کیا گیا تھا جہاں وہ جانبر نہ ہو سکی۔ مبینہ تشدد کا یہ واقعہ پولیس لائنز میں پیش آیا اور اس سلسلے میں تھانہ شمس کالونی میں مقدمہ درج کیا گیا۔

پولیس کے مطابق اس واقعے میں ملوث پولیس افسر کی اہلیہ اور ایک گھریلو ملازم کو گرفتار کر لیا گیا ہے۔ گرفتار ہونے والی خاتون غیر ملکی شہریت بھی رکھتی ہیں اور تفتیشی ٹیم کے ایک اہلکار کے مطابق مقتولہ ان کی رشتہ دار بھی تھی۔ مقتولہ کا پوسٹ مارٹم مکمل کر لیا گیا ہے اور اس کی ابتدائی رپورٹ پولیس کو موصول ہونے کی توقع ہے۔

متعلقہ پولیس افسر محمد بن اشرف ماضی میں اسلام آباد پولیس ہیڈ کوارٹر میں ایس پی کے طور پر تعینات رہے ہیں اور اسی دوران انہیں پولیس لائنز میں رہائش گاہ الاٹ کی گئی تھی۔ واقعے کے وقت وہ ایف آئی اے گوجرانوالہ ریجن میں بطور ڈائریکٹر خدمات انجام دے رہے تھے۔ اسلام آباد پولیس کے ترجمان نے بتایا کہ مقدمے کے مدعی مقتولہ کے والد ہیں جنہوں نے اپنی درخواست میں کسی فرد کا نام شامل نہیں کیا، البتہ تفتیش اور شواہد کی بنیاد پر ملزمان کو نامزد کیا جا سکے گا۔

اسلام آباد پولیس کے ڈی آئی جی ہیڈ کوارٹر جواد طارق کا کہنا ہے کہ پولیس لائنز میں متعدد افسران کے گھر موجود ہیں اور پولیس اس وقت تک اندرونی معاملات میں مداخلت نہیں کرتی جب تک کوئی باضابطہ شکایت موصول نہ ہو۔ پولیس کا کہنا ہے کہ واقعے کی شفاف تحقیقات کی جا رہی ہیں اور پوسٹ مارٹم رپورٹ کی روشنی میں مزید قانونی کارروائی عمل میں لائی جائے گی۔

stories.title: وفاقی آئینی عدالت نے پی ٹی آئی کی درخواست پر حکم میں ترمیم کر دی
stories.summary:
خیبرپختونخوا میں تین ایم پی او کے تحت گرفتاریوں سے متعلق کیس میں وفاقی آئینی عدالت نے پاکستان تحریک انصاف کی درخواست منظور کرتے ہوئے پانچ نومبر کے اپنے حکم میں ترمیم کر دی ہے۔ چیف جسٹس وفاقی آئینی عدالت جسٹس امین الدین خان اور جسٹس عامر فاروق پر مشتمل بینچ نے اس کیس کی سماعت کی۔ سماعت کے دوران چیئرمین پی ٹی آئی بیرسٹر گوہر نے موقف اختیار کیا کہ عدالت کے پہلے والے حکم سے پشاور ہائیکورٹ کی کارروائی اور وکلا کی پریکٹس متاثر ہوئی ہے۔ وفاقی آئینی عدالت اس معاملے سے متعلق متفرق درخواستوں پر جمعرات کو سماعت کرے گی۔

عدالت نے اپنے ریمارکس میں واضح کیا کہ حکم امتناع گورنر راج اور ایم پی او سے متعلق معاملات تک محدود تھا جبکہ پشاور ہائیکورٹ آئین کے آرٹیکل 199 کے تحت دیگر مقدمات کی سماعت جاری رکھ سکتی ہے۔ اس دوران عدالت نے پشاور بار کونسل کو بھی مقدمے میں فریق بننے کی اجازت دے دی۔ دو رکنی بینچ نے اس حوالے سے فیصلہ جاری کیا۔ اس کیس کی سماعت کے دوران مختلف قانونی اور آئینی نکات زیر بحث آئے جن میں عدالتی دائرہ اختیار اور مختلف آرٹیکلز کی تشریح شامل تھی۔

اسی دوران ملک کے دیگر حصوں اور خبروں میں فضائی آلودگی کا مسئلہ بدستور برقرار ہے جہاں دنیا کے بڑے شہروں میں لاہور آلودگی کے لحاظ سے دوسرے اور کراچی چھٹے نمبر پر موجود ہے۔ استور میں وقفے وقفے سے بارش اور برفباری سے سردی میں اضافہ ہو گیا ہے جبکہ کراچی سے لاہور جانے والی پروازوں میں گھنٹوں تاخیر کے باعث مسافروں کو مشکلات کا سامنا کرنا پڑا۔ دوسری جانب اسلام آباد میں اقتصادی تعاون تنظیم کے تیسرے وزرائے خارجہ کے اجلاس کا ایجنڈا طے کر لیا گیا ہے اور اس سلسلے میں مہمان وزرائے خارجہ اور وفود کی آمد کا سلسلہ بھی جاری ہے۔

stories.title: England Edges Spain While Belgium Thumps Italy in Nations League Action
stories.summary:
England ended Spain's impressive 44-match unbeaten run in competitive fixtures on Sunday by securing a 3-2 victory in Madrid under coach Thomas Tuchel. Harry Kane opened the scoring from the penalty spot just before halftime to net his record-extending 93rd international goal for England. Ezri Konsa and Ben White added further goals after the break, with White finishing between Unai Simon's legs following a pass from Jude Bellingham. Despite finishing the match with 10 men after Elliot Anderson received a red card for conceding a penalty, England held on against a late Spanish fightback featuring goals from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams to win Group A3.

In Group A1, Belgium overturned a deficit to thrash Italy 4-1 and claim a spot in the Nations League quarter-finals. Francesco Pio Esposito had initially put Italy ahead with an 11th-minute volley, but Belgium quickly responded through Maxim De Cuyper, Nathan Ngoy, and Jeremy Doku. Diego Moreira sealed the scoreline with a late strike, while goalkeeper Senne Lammens saved a weak penalty from Esposito in the dying moments. The defeat left Italian manager Roberto Mancini reflecting on a painful rebuilding process, as his team missed out on a crucial draw needed to advance.

France secured the top spot in Group A1 by defeating Turkey 2-1 in Bordeaux, bouncing back from an earlier loss to Italy. Zinedine Zidane's squad capitalized on an own goal by Emirhan Topcu and a strike from Eli Junior Kroupi, ensuring they enter Friday's quarter-final draw in Nyon, Switzerland, as a seeded team. This seeding guarantees that Les Bleus will host the return leg of the quarter-finals in March 2027, though it leaves open the possibility of facing Spain.

Separately, the governments of Australia, Britain, Canada, and Italy issued a joint statement on Sunday calling on Israel to immediately permit rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza. The four nations described the conditions on the ground as dire and urged the Israeli government to halt ongoing delays in delivering vital aid to the region.

stories.title: Russian air defenses intercept over 100 drones targeting Moscow overnight
stories.summary:
Russian air defense systems intercepted more than 100 drones aimed at Moscow overnight, according to the capital's mayor, Sergey Sobyanin. Writing on Telegram, Sobyanin reported that approximately 139 drones were intercepted in total through the night and into Monday morning, with emergency service personnel deployed to areas where debris landed. This aerial assault followed recent Ukrainian strikes targeting a major Russian petrochemical facility, an oil refinery, and a military manufacturing site.

The drone interceptions occurred just days before a scheduled summit in Shenzhen, China, where Russian President Vladimir Putin is set to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. China verified that Xi will host the talks on November 19 on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, though Beijing did not release an agenda.

U.S. officials indicated that while President Trump intends to address nuclear arms reduction and the conflict involving Iran during the trilateral discussions, the nearly five-year war between Russia and Ukraine is not expected to be a topic. Instead, Washington is pursuing separate diplomatic negotiations involving Kyiv and Moscow to resolve the conflict. Meanwhile, German President Frank-German President Frank-Frank-Frank-Steinmeier noted that President Xi recently expressed irritation regarding suggestions to include the Ukraine war in the trilateral format, stressing it is a European conflict requiring European participation.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed concern that the upcoming Shenzhen meeting could mirror the 1945 Yalta conference, potentially leading major powers to negotiate spheres of influence without smaller nations present at the negotiating table.

stories.title: ICC announces 2028-2031 tournament hosts as India, England, Australia, and New Zealand sweep events
stories.summary:
The International Cricket Council released its schedule for the 2028-2035 cycle, revealing that India, England, Australia, and New Zealand will host all marquee events scheduled between 2028 and 2031. Venues for matches taking place from 2032 to 2035 will be determined at a later date. Notably, Pakistan—which successfully hosted an eight-tier Champions Trophy tournament last year—was not awarded any hosting duties for the upcoming cycle.

Under the newly approved schedule, Australia and New Zealand will co-host the 2028 T20 World Cup. India will host the 2029 ICC Champions Trophy and jointly organize the 2031 ICC World Cup alongside Bangladesh. England is set to hold the ICC Test Championship final in both 2029 and 2030, and will also share hosting duties for the 2030 T20 World Cup with Ireland and Scotland. The governing body stated that these choices aim to expand opportunities for full and associate members while strengthening qualification pathways.

In addition to tournament hosts, the ICC outlined various qualification structures. The 2027 Men’s World Cup Qualifier in February and March will feature 10 teams divided into two groups of five, culminating in semi-finals and a final. A separate 16-team Global Qualifier in early 2028 will determine eight direct participants for the 2028 Men’s T20 World Cup. For the women's pathway, the Netherlands and Scotland will join eight regional qualifiers in a global tournament to secure the final two spots for the 2028 ICC Women’s T20 World Cup.

Furthermore, host nations and dates were finalized for the last qualification phase for cricket's return to the Olympics at the Los Angeles 2028 Games. The men’s qualifier will take place from February 5 to 13, 2028, in Bangladesh, while the women’s event is scheduled from February 26 to March 5, 2028, in the United States. Each tournament will comprise eight teams competing for a single qualification berth.

stories.title: Karachi water shortages persist despite maintenance completion at Dhabeji pumping station
stories.summary:
Residents in multiple neighborhoods across Karachi experienced water shortages for a third consecutive day on Sunday, even though the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation announced the completion of annual maintenance work at the Dhabeji pumping station. The utility previously warned that maintenance activities starting November 13 would result in a daily supply shortfall of roughly 130 million gallons. On Sunday, officials confirmed that all 21 pumps at Dhabeji were fully operational and that overall city supply had been restored.

According to the utility's statement, technical tasks such as valve installations and pipeline repairs were successfully concluded. Water distribution to impacted sectors, including Landhi, Korangi, Malir, and Shah Faisal towns, was reportedly being gradually normalized. However, the agency's announcement did not specify a exact timeline for when full service would resume for all affected consumers.

A KWSC spokesperson detailed that various improvements were executed during the operation to boost the efficiency and stability of the water network.
